content:
Meeting header
Date/time: 2026-06-10 11:00am PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Rivera (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Head of Security, Cascade Systems), Priya Desai (Eng Mgr), Jorge Ramirez (Platform Ops)

Summary:
High-level security review focused on SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning flows, RBAC/least-privilege role model, audit log retention and KMS integration for Redwood Private/Dedicated options. Cascade wants a clear provisioning pattern for their org units, confirmation on encrypted keys/HSM support, and sample assertions/claims. Team agreed to a short pilot to exercise SCIM group pushes and auditing.

Topics:
- SAML attributes / NameID and group claims
- SCIM group mapping and filtering (orgUnit / team hierarchy)
- RBAC role model + least privilege templates
- Service accounts, API keys, and ephemeral credentials
- KMS/HSM integration & envelope encryption for private deployments
- Audit logs, retention, and evidence for SOC 2
- Data residency and on-prem considerations

Action items (see metadata)

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm ethan, AE on the account. maya is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Liam (Cascade): hi all, liam here, head of security at cascade. we got priya and jorge on the line too.
[00:18] Priya (Cascade): hey, yep.
[00:20] Maya (Redwood SE): great, thanks. real quick agenda—saml, scim, rbac patterns, then k m s and audit logs. sound right?
[00:29] Jorge (Cascade): yep that's exactly it. we're mainly trying to nail down least-privilege and how provisioning will behave for our teams.
[00:36] Ethan: perfect. to start, does cascade currently use a central IdP or multiple?
[00:40] Liam: central okta tenant for engineers, but marketing uses azure ad. long story. for this pilot we want to focus on okta and group-based provisioning.
[00:50] Maya: okta is straightforward—SCIM push and SAML app. we usually ask for a group claim in the SAML assertion, or we do SCIM group sync. either works but scim is stronger for full lifecycle.
[01:03] Priya: quick Q—if we push groups via scim, can we filter by orgUnit? we have nested teams and don't want all groups mapped.
[01:10] Maya: yes, scim supports filtering. on our side you can configure a mapping rule like urn:enterprise:orgUnit => team, and then map that to a redwood role. we do see customers want a single source of truth so scim is preferred when possible.
[01:24] Jorge: ok, and for SAML attributes—what do you expect? nameid? email? group claim?
[01:29] Maya: we accept NameID/email. for groups we check the group claim (usually groups or member_of). if groups are large we recommend sending group IDs instead of full names to avoid token bloat. also include an attribute for employeeType or role for initial seeding.
[01:44] Liam: any limits on claim size? last vendor we tried truncated group lists.
[01:49] Maya: the short answer is yes, assertion size is a constraint. that's why SCIM is preferred for big orgs. for SAML we can do a lookup from an id (group id) to a group name via SCIM post-provision call.
[02:05] Ethan: from a security posture perspective, Cascade asked about least-privilege templates—what's typical?
[02:12] Maya: we recommend a 4-role baseline: Org Admin (very limited, mostly billing/owner), Security Admin (audit + key management), Platform Ops (deploy/run models), and App Developers (invoke endpoints). avoid giving model upload or infra create to devs unless needed.
[02:27] Priya: can those map to scim groups automatically? our wish is: scim group 'platform-ops' => Redwood role 'Platform Ops'.
[02:34] Maya: yes, that's the standard. you can set group-to-role mapping in the console or via scim group metadata. and you can have multiple groups map to a single role.
[02:42] Jorge: what about service accounts? we have CI pipelines that need programmatic access. how do we control scope?
[02:48] Maya: service accounts are treated as identities with their own RBAC. we recommend creating dedicated scim/group for CI service accounts, give them minimal token scopes, and rotate keys frequently. for Dedicated/Private we support short lived tokens and you can integrate with your vault for ephemeral creds.
[03:05] Liam: is there an HSM/KMS integration for key wrapping? we can't store plaintext customer keys.
[03:10] Maya: yes—Redwood Private supports BYOK via customer KMS. we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for on-prem. we do envelope encryption: model artifacts and logs encrypted at rest with data keys wrapped by your KMS. for hosted we manage keys but you can opt for dedicated key control with enterprise contracts.
[03:28] Liam: good. audit logs—what fields do you capture and can we push them to our SIEM?
[03:34] Maya: audit logs include actor, action, resource, timestamp, token_id, request metadata (ip, region), and a redacted payload. we can forward logs to your S3 bucket or push via syslog/forwarder to Splunk/Datadog. retention is configurable; default is 90 days for hosted. for SOC 2 customers we offer longer retention as an add-on.
[03:56] Priya: we need tamper-evidence and exportable proofs for audits. how do you provide evidence?
[04:02] Ethan: we provide audit exports, signed log bundles, and for Private Dedicated we can enable WORM buckets that are customer-managed. the SOC 2 report includes controls we map to actions. we'll share the one-pager.
[04:14] Liam: speaking of SOC 2/ISO, do you have certs? any gap areas we should be aware of?
[04:19] Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and pursuing ISO 27001. our public security docs list the scope. things customers often ask about: data residency—where logs and blobs live for hosted endpoints. we can pin regions for data residency and with Private you can keep everything in your VPC.
[04:36] Jorge: for the pilot—can we start with a staging deployment where scim pushes 50 users and we validate role mappings and audit logs?
[04:43] Maya: absolutely. recommended flow: redwood shares saml metadata + scim schema, cascade configures an Okta app + SCIM connector in staging, redwood enables a test org, run push, then we both validate logs.
[04:55] Priya: timeline—how fast can we get that?
[04:58] Ethan: if we exchange artifacts this week, we can do pilot next Tuesday. maya, is that realistic?
[05:03] Maya: yes, i'll send metadata today and can be on the kickoff. testing will probably take a day or two.
[05:09] Liam: excellent.
[05:11] Jorge: question on least-privilege enforcement—if someone accidentally belongs to multiple groups that map to higher privilege, is there a deny list or precedence?
[05:20] Maya: good question. our system uses role precedence rules in the console—explicit deny at group mapping is supported but we suggest avoiding denies unless needed. you can set precedence so higher-security roles override others. we also support automated audits that flag privilege escalation when group membership changes.
[05:37] Priya: are those audits available via the API? we want to schedule nightly checks.
[05:41] Maya: yes, audit API and event stream. you can pull events or subscribe via webhooks. most customers consume into their SIEM for automated alerts.
[05:50] Ethan: any data residency red flags—Cascade mentioned EU customers, need EU logging.
[05:55] Liam: right we need EU-only storage for EU customers. we also need to ensure egress controls for logs.
[06:01] Maya: we can pin the region and separate buckets per region. for hosted customers you can request EU-only quotas and storage. Dedicated/Private gives full control.
[06:09] Jorge: encryption at rest—are DB snapshots encrypted with customer keys?
[06:13] Maya: for private and dedicated yes, snapshots and backups can be wrapped with your KMS. for hosted managed keys we rotate under our process, but can provide audit evidence.
[06:22] Liam: ok. procurement may ask for a data flow diagram and a list of sub-processors. can you provide that?
[06:28] Ethan: yes, we'll attach the data flow diagram and sub-processor list to the follow-up email.
[06:32] Priya: another small thing—SCIM group names might contain slashes in our org pattern, do you normalize?
[06:38] Maya: we canonicalize group names; slashes are allowed but we map them to safe ids. we can also pass raw metadata in scim extensions so you keep original path.
[06:47] Jorge: for service account rotation—does Redwood support automatic key rotation with our vault?
[06:52] Maya: we integrate with HashiCorp Vault for secrets and can rotate service tokens via the vault plugin. for cloud KMS we have native rotation hooks.
[06:59] Liam: great. any limitations on SCIM attribute types? we have custom attributes like cost_center.
[07:05] Maya: SCIM supports custom attrs; we accept extensions and you can map them in the console. cost_center is a common one for tagging.
[07:12] Ethan: let's talk about SAML failure modes—if assertion fails, do you fall back to a manual provisioning UI?
[07:18] Maya: yes, failures surface in the Admin UI with suggested fixes. you can approve manually or re-trigger scim sync. we also emit detailed failure codes for SAML parse errors.
[07:28] Priya: one-more question—are personal tokens visible in the audit log? we shouldn't see secrets in logs.
[07:33] Maya: we never log full secrets. token IDs are logged (prefixes) but secrets are redacted. access to raw secrets is gated and audited.
[07:42] Jorge: ok this is good. we need to validate the audit chain for one of our previous incidents—would you allow a joint replay of events for the pilot?
[07:51] Maya: yes, once the pilot is set we'll export the event stream and you can replay in staging. we'll coordinate the export permissions.
[07:58] Ethan: let's capture next steps—maya will send artifacts, priya will share the RBAC matrix, jorge will provision the test app. any other asks?
[08:07] Liam: please include the SOC2 control mappings for authn/authz in that one-pager.
[08:12] Ethan: will do.
[08:14] Priya: timeline again—monday artifacts, pilot tuesday-wednesday?
[08:18] Maya: yes, aiming for pilot next tuesday. we'll send calendar invites.
[08:22] Jorge: ok thanks everyone.
[08:24] Ethan: thanks all—closing now.

End of transcript
